content:
The Webb County Attorney’s Office says it is seeing a growing number of cases involving minors found with firearms — and officials are urging parents to pay closer attention, KGNS reported.

First Assistant County Attorney Rolando Garza said teens are often passing or selling weapons to one another for a few dollars without considering the consequences. The office recently handled a case involving a 14-year-old found with a firearm inside his home, and in another recent case, two 16-year-olds were shot by another teenager.

The office’s anti-gang unit is monitoring how the weapons are being passed around, and Garza flagged a growing concern about teens accessing stolen or illegal weapons through social media and the dark web.

“Another problem is, of course, parents who do have weapons that they make sure are secure, that they have them locked and that their children do not have access to those weapons as well,” Garza told KGNS.

Sources: KGNS, “Webb County Attorney’s Office warns of rise in minors found with firearms,” by Ruby Villarreal, Oct. 23, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: The Webb County Attorney's Office says more minors are being found with firearms — including a 14-year-old caught with one at home — and warns parents to lock up their weapons as teens trade guns for a few dollars.
title: County Attorney's Office warns of growing number of minors found with firearms
